summary: The paper studies three training-free uncertainty-quantification signals (mean max-token-probability, negative predictive entropy, self-consistency) plus a logistic combination and a from-scratch linear hidden-state probe, for predicting correctness of a tiny (~50K-parameter) decoder-only transformer trained to do integer addition, arguing this avoids the LLM-judge confound present in open-domain semantic-entropy evaluations. On the seed=0 main run all signals discriminate well (AUROC 0.84-0.87), self-consistency is miscalibrated (ECE 0.088) but fixable by isotonic recalibration or the logistic combo (ECE 0.042-0.055), and confidence-based abstention raises retained-set accuracy from 65.4% to 81-90% depending on coverage. This revision directly responds to four round-1 reviewers by adding a 5-seed robustness sweep (showing self-consistency's AUROC is unstable, 0.59-0.94, and that the main run's signal ranking is not robust) and a new hidden-state linear probe, and by correcting two previously overstated claims (the 70%-coverage accuracy figure and the timing claim).
strengths:
- I reran experiment.py end-to-end (fresh process) and it reproduced the paper's exact reported AUROCs (0.871/0.863/0.841/0.874), ECEs (0.088/0.055/0.042), and per-digit/per-carry accuracy tables to 3+ decimal places, confirming the main-run numbers are not cherry-picked or misreported
- The paper is unusually transparent about its own revision history: it explicitly names the four prior-round critiques (single-seed ranking claims, missing hidden-state-probe baseline, overstated coverage phrasing, unreproducible timing) and shows concretely how each was addressed (Sections 3-4), rather than just asserting improvement
- The 5-seed sweep is a genuinely informative addition rather than a token gesture: it overturns part of the main-run narrative (self-consistency is *not* reliably the weakest signal — it wins outright in 1/5 seeds and mean-max-prob beats it in only 4/5), and the paper reports this candidly instead of suppressing it
- The controlled, ground-truth-exact testbed is a reasonable and clearly-scoped methodological device for isolating UQ-signal quality from judge quality, and the paper is careful to bound its claims to the qualitative pattern rather than claiming the absolute numbers transfer to frontier LLMs
weaknesses:
- The 5-seed robustness table's stated range for neg-mean-entropy ("0.826-0.925") does not match the paper's own robustness_results.json, whose five seed values are {0.881, 0.889, 0.838, 0.925, 0.852} — the true minimum is 0.838, not 0.826 (I verified this directly against the JSON file shipped with the paper). This is a real, checkable numerical error in a table that otherwise correctly reports every other signal's range (mean-max-prob, self-consistency, logistic-combo, and hidden-state-probe ranges all matched the underlying data exactly when I checked them)
- The contribution is narrow in scope by the paper's own admission (a 3-layer, 64-dim model on 1-4 digit addition), and while this is an appropriate and clearly-stated limitation rather than overclaiming, it does mean the paper's generalizable takeaway is fairly thin: "mean-max-prob and entropy are consistently strong, self-consistency is seed-sensitive" is a plausible but not deeply surprising finding, and no experiment establishes whether the qualitative pattern actually holds at LLM scale (the one place a real LLM could have been touched, e.g. by checking whether digit-addition-style trends replicate on a small pretrained model, is left as future work)
- The 5-seed sweep uses a substantially different (reduced) configuration than the main run (400 test examples vs 2,000, ~3% vs 65.4% greedy accuracy), so it is honestly reported as answering only the narrower seed-stability question rather than validating the headline AUROC numbers themselves — but this also means the paper's central claim (mean-max-prob is "the best single signal" at AUROC 0.871) is still ultimately a single-seed number with no confirmed variance at the scale it's reported at
questions:
1. Can you correct the neg-mean-entropy range in the 5-seed table (Section 3) to 0.838-0.925 per the values in robustness_results.json, or clarify if a different definition of "range" (e.g. excluding an outlier) was intended?
2. Have you tried running the 5-seed sweep at the main run's full scale (2,000 test examples, 6 epochs) rather than the reduced configuration, even for just 2-3 seeds, to check whether the seed-instability finding for self-consistency persists at the accuracy level the main-run AUROC numbers are actually reported at?
3. Is there a plan (even informally) to check whether the qualitative ranking (mean-max-prob/entropy stable, self-consistency volatile) holds on a small real pretrained LLM on a toy exact-match task (e.g. simple string reversal or lookup), to bridge between this fully synthetic setting and the open-domain literature it's positioned against?
